source.title: Is network fragmentation a useful complexity measure?
source.authors: Coenraad Mouton; Randle Rabe; Daniël G. Haasbroek; Marthinus W. Theunissen; H. L. Potgieter; M. Davel

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure data are not numerically transcribed in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study runs a model-capacity sweep and measures test error, explicitly reporting a double-descent result in its label-corrupted setting. This directly tests model-wise double descent, using a setup described as similar to the standard CNN setup in prior work.
record.gate_note: The study also measures fragmentation and reports its correlation with test or validation error, but those fragmentation scores do not themselves measure the error curves named in the claim versions. Its PGDL results concern generalization-gap ranking, not a size, epoch, or sample-size double-descent sweep. The reported training-time error plots do not explicitly establish epoch-wise double descent.
record.test_reason: The study's main aim is fragmentation as a complexity measure. It still trains a Nakkiran-style CNN width sweep (k=4–64) on CIFAR10 with 10% label noise and reports the test-error curve. The text states 'we observe a pronounced DD for the label-corrupted models'. That is a close-recipe check of model-wise double descent (V1), though an incidental one.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that fragmentation tracks test error in the controlled double-descent setting and is competitive as a generalization predictor on PGDL. They say its mechanisms remain unknown and that it is not explained by large weight norms.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies CNN capacity and measures error as in a model-wise double-descent test, using an architecture similar to a prior standard CNN setup. It compares clean and 10% label-corrupted CIFAR10 training data and reports three initialization seeds; the text does not establish an exact reproduction of the original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different training-data conditions (clean versus 10% label-corrupted); its double-descent result is explicitly described for the label-corrupted condition. It also evaluates selected training checkpoints, but does not report epoch-wise double descent in error.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-space and hidden-layer decision-region fragmentation follows the test-error double-descent curve over width. It peaks in the interpolation regime, is higher for label-corrupted models, and tracks validation error during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decision-boundary fragmentation peaks at the interpolation threshold and mirrors the double-descent test-error curve.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Scientific Methods for Understanding Deep Learning, NeurIPS 2024
record.problems: The test-error values are available only in a figure and are not numerically transcribed. The text explicitly describes pronounced double descent for corrupted data but does not describe the clean-data curve's shape. The study uses one image dataset and a CNN family for the controlled sweep.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing rows were left out. Fragmentation scores, PGDL ranking results, weight norms, and validation-error trajectories were not included because they do not directly measure the error curves named by the tested versions.

untested.parts: Other architectures and datasets; a numerical peak height or location. The text says only that models interpolate for k>9 (clean) and k>11 (corrupt).
Whether the peak shrinks or vanishes without label noise (clean curve not described); variance; multiple descent; optimal regularization.
Figure 5 plots validation error over 1000 epochs for k=4, 10, 64, but the text never describes a fall-rise-fall shape.
Fragmentation is proposed as a complexity measure, but it is not shown to predict peak location across axes.

missing.what: Interpolation thresholds: all models with k>9 (clean) and k>11 (corrupt) reach 0% train error. This places the test-error peak region near k≈10.
Training and validation error trajectories over 1000 epochs for k=4, 10, 64, clean versus corrupt. The shape is not described in the text and is figure only.

record.verdict_notes: Double descent is reproduced as a setting for studying fragmentation, not as the object of study. All test-error evidence is figure-only, and the authors call the result 'as expected'. The PGDL and weight-norm results are rightly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Other model families and datasets; an exact numerical location of the peak relative to the interpolation threshold.
The study plots validation error during training but does not report that error follows a fall-rise-fall double-descent shape over epochs.
No training-sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across general model classes testing a general double-descent curve.
No test of whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study compares clean and label-corrupted training data, but does not test variance as a driver, triple or multiple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameter number or test of whether that makes the second descent an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.value: figure only; the text reports a pronounced double descent for the label-corrupted models
rows.note: The result is reported as a capacity-sweep curve, not as a numerical value for an individual width. The text states that the label-corrupted models show pronounced double descent; the plot's point values are not available in the extracted text.
rows.check: Linked to V1 only. V6 needs a clean-versus-noisy contrast in the size of the peak, and the text never describes the clean curve. A single noisy-condition curve cannot show that noise drives the peak.

relationships.condition: CNN width sweep on CIFAR10 with 10% label noise, Adam, 500 epochs
relationships.reason: The authors report pronounced double descent in test error versus width for label-corrupted models (r1). The evidence is figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Test error exhibited pronounced double descent across widths with 10% label noise.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
